title: The secret scanner detects cardholder data

role_assignments._run_id_disambiguation: /claude/r0_steward (Anthropic) is THIS package's Integration Owner and must record its own capability declaration before this package leaves backlog. /root/r0_steward (OpenAI Codex) is a DIFFERENT run: it is the Integration Owner of WP-0A-A0-001 and WP-0A-CON-001 and is named in open_blockers solely because it must countersign the amendments made to those two packages and record the WP-0A-CON-001 npm run check addendum. Neither run substitutes for the other. Independent testing flagged the near-identical names as ambiguous; both are intended.

independence.cross_vendor_exception: prefer_cross_vendor_review is NOT satisfied: every assigned run is Anthropic claude-opus-5. The Decision Register (§ cross-vendor review) permits this only as an explicit exception - 'if there is no cross-vendor capacity, use an independent agent per run and record the exception'. Each of the five roles is a separate agent run with its own capability declaration and no run reviewed, tested, or integrated its own work. The Integration Owner must carry this exception forward; it is not waived and it is not equivalent to cross-vendor review.

required_human_authorities: Product Owner disposition of RFC-2026-008 before the manual merge described in RFC-2026-002
purpose: scripts/scan-repository-secrets.mjs carries thirty credential rules and three privacy rules, and not one of them detects a payment card number. A payment provider is one of this repository's own declared Gate G0 blockers, so the first credential this repository is likely to meet in anger is the one class it cannot see. CONTRIBUTING_AGENTS.md forbids customer PII repository-wide with no carve-out; a primary account number is customer PII and a scanner that reports a Thai national identity number while ignoring a card number enforces that rule selectively.

include: One scan rule detecting a primary account number by Luhn checksum and issuer prefix together
RFC-2026-008 recording the decision, including why published provider test cards are reported rather than exempted
Test coverage in test-kits/secret-scan.test.mjs, including the false-positive cases the rule must NOT report
exclude: Any provider integration, sandbox credential or live key -- Gate G0 forbids all three
A card verification value rule: three digits carry no checksum and no prefix, so a rule for them reports noise and would be disabled
A Thai bank account number rule: the format carries no checksum this scanner can verify
Any change to what npm run check runs, or to any contract

amends_without_owning.rationale: WP-0A-A0-003 owns the scanner and its test; WP-0A-A0-002 owns the integrity manifest. This package adds one rule and its coverage, and updates the digests it necessarily invalidates. Declaring these as outputs made the ownership validator exit 70, correctly: two packages cannot hold one path. The amendment is recorded on the owning manifests instead. The workflow and the manifests below were carried up the stack so every downstream pull request runs the same branch-scope step; .github/workflows/ci.yml belongs to WP-0A-A0-004 and each manifest to its own package.

acceptance_criteria: A Luhn-valid card number carrying a recognised issuer prefix is reported, in prose and in code alike.
A Luhn-INVALID digit run of card length is not reported, so a correlation id or a hash prefix does not become a finding.
A Luhn-valid run with no recognised issuer prefix is not reported: one in ten arbitrary digit runs passes Luhn, and a rule that fires on those is noise.
A published provider test card IS reported. The scanner cannot distinguish a test number from a live one at rest, and Gate G0 permits no provider integration that would need one.
The rule is not prose-exempt, on the same footing as the Thai national identity rule.
Repository scan over the tree stays clean; npm run check stays green with no test skipped.
required_tests: Positive: each supported issuer family, hyphen- and space-separated forms
Negative: Luhn-invalid runs, repeated-digit fillers, unrecognised prefixes, and adjacent-digit boundaries
The published provider test card is reported
rollback_or_forward_fix: Revert through a reviewed revert PR. One scan rule and its tests; no persisted data, provider state, credential, migration or customer-data effect.
open_blockers: RFC-2026-008 is Proposed and requires Product Owner disposition before the RFC-2026-002 manual merge.
A pattern scanner cannot prove absence. This closes one named class; it does not make the scanner complete, and the 37 of 56 uncorrelated decoys recorded against WP-0A-A0-003 remain unreported.

When a Stripe sandbox is authorized and a G0 blocker lifts, fixture work may legitimately need a test card. That must arrive as a reviewed exemption with a named owner, not as an allowlist added quietly to this rule.
